- Milestone: M0
- Branch / worktree: `t/M0-2b`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M0-2b`
- Depends on: M0-2a (merged), BA-3/BA-4 (redefined 2026-10-29: Cloudflare Tunnel, see STATE.md Decisions)
- Touches (exclusive while running): `spikes/mcp/`, `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md`. On hoid: `~/finbot-spike/mcp/` only, plus
  docker containers/images/volumes/networks whose names start with `finbot-spike`
- Plan refs: architecture.md §4; read `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md` §8 (the M0-2b checklist) and

## Goal
The M0-2a hello server runs on hoid and is publicly reachable at `https://finance.hoidlabs.site`. Brendan adds it to
claude.ai as a custom connector, signs in with Google and calls `hello` from Claude web and mobile. The output is a running
spike plus the real-connector findings that settle U9.

## Setup facts (verified by sup 2026-10-29)
- **The exposure plan changed:**
  - hoid's router does not forward 80/443: `https://hoidlabs.site` is refused from outside. So **no nginx, no
    nginx-proxy-manager, no certbot, no sudo**.
  - `hoidlabs.site` DNS is on Cloudflare (nameservers switched).
  - Brendan created a Cloudflare Tunnel `hoid` with the public hostname `finance.hoidlabs.site` → `HTTP` → `finbot:8080`.
  - Cloudflare terminates TLS.
- **Token:** hoid `~/finbot/.env` (perms 600) holds `CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN` (a valid tunnel token) and
  `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
  - Never print either.
  - Don't give the finbot container that whole file: it must not see the claude token. Pass only the variables each
    container needs.
- **What's already on hoid** (leave all of it alone):
  - docker 29.9.2, compose v5.6.1;
  - system nginx on 80/443;
  - an unused nginx-proxy-manager container;
  - chore-chart and ledger containers on host ports 8080/8081/3001.
  
  None of them may be touched. **Don't publish any host port** for finbot; cloudflared reaches it over the compose network.
- **Google client:** has both redirect URIs: `http://localhost:8080/oauth/google/callback` and
  `https://finance.hoidlabs.site/oauth/google/callback`. Consent screen Testing, 2 test users.
- **Secrets for the server:**
  - `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` and `MCP_ALLOWED_EMAILS` (Brendan only) are in your worktree `.env`.
  - Copy just those keys to hoid as `~/finbot-spike/mcp/mcp.env` (perms 600), streamed over ssh stdin. Never put them on
    argv, and never echo them.
- sup's call for this spike: logins are lost on redeploy (in-memory fosite store). Persistence is M3 work.
  Don't add SQL storage here.

## Scope
- **Compose project `finbot-spike`** in `~/finbot-spike/mcp/` on hoid. Build the image on hoid from `spikes/mcp`: copy the
  source with `rsync`/`scp`; no registry. Use a small multi-stage Dockerfile under `spikes/mcp/`.
  - **Service `finbot`:**
    - `MCP_LISTEN_ADDR=:8080` and `MCP_PUBLIC_URL=https://finance.hoidlabs.site`;
    - a named volume for `MCP_DATA_DIR`;
    - `env_file: mcp.env`;
    - no `ports:`;
    - `restart: unless-stopped`.
    
    Mind agy r3's note: the go-sdk loopback guard must not trigger on the `finance.hoidlabs.site` Host header.
  - **Service `cloudflared`:**
    - image `cloudflare/cloudflared`, pinned to an exact version tag;
    - `tunnel --no-autoupdate run`, with `TUNNEL_TOKEN` taken from `CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN`;
    - wire it so the token isn't visible in `docker inspect` args (an env var is fine; `--token` on the command line is not);
    - `restart: unless-stopped`.
- **Work through `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md` §8 items 1–6**, adapted for Cloudflare instead of NPM:
  - item 3 becomes: Cloudflare passes `Authorization` through, SSE/streaming works through the tunnel, and `/.well-known/*`
    is served by finbot;
  - item 4: check the endpoints answer from outside within 10 s;
  - check Cloudflare doesn't put a challenge or bot-fight page in front of Anthropic's or OpenAI's callers. If it does,
    note the exact dashboard setting for Brendan.
- **Outside checks:** from this Mac (DNS now resolves via Cloudflare, so no hairpin problem):
  - `curl -i https://finance.hoidlabs.site/mcp` → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`;
  - both well-known documents show `https://finance.hoidlabs.site` in issuer/resource.
- **Real connectors** (Brendan does them, guided by you): when the server is up, append
  `QUESTION M0-2b: please add the connector` with exact steps:
  - claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, URL `https://finance.hoidlabs.site/mcp`, then Google sign-in,
    consent page, Allow;
  - then, in a chat, ask Claude to call `hello`;
  - then the Claude mobile app, using the same connector.
  
  Wait for the answer (poll your log, don't spin). Then ask for a ChatGPT developer-mode attempt if Brendan has a plan that
  allows it, and record the result either way. Gemini only if trivially available.
- **Revoke on hoid:** `docker compose exec finbot … revoke <email>`, run without printing the email (read it from the env
  file inside the container, or pass `--all`). Show that the next tool call from claude.ai fails, and record what the client
  does.
- Update `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md` with a "Deployed on hoid (M0-2b)" section:
  - the compose layout;
  - each §8 item VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED;
  - the connector results per client (this settles U9);
  - the RFC 9207 `iss` answer for ChatGPT if you reached it;
  - "Impact on architecture": §4 exposure is now a Cloudflare Tunnel, not nginx-proxy-manager. Note what that means for
    "rate-limit + fail2ban at the proxy" (Cloudflare rate-limiting rules instead).
- Leave it **running** at the end. sup decides when to take it down.

## Out of scope
- sudo, the system nginx, nginx-proxy-manager, router or firewall changes. The other containers on hoid. `~/finbot/.env`
  (read the tunnel token from it; don't edit it).
- Cloudflare dashboard changes: Brendan makes them. Ask via QUESTION, with exact clicks.
- Persistent token storage, real finbot tools, YNAB, the root module, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plan/*`.
- Committing tokens, emails, client ids, the tunnel id or account ids.

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `spikes/mcp/Dockerfile` and `.dockerignore`: multi-stage build, golang:1.26-alpine → distroless/static:nonroot, with
    `/data` owned by nonroot for the named volume.
  - `spikes/mcp/deploy/compose.yaml`: project `finbot-spike` with `finbot` (`:8080`, public URL, volume, `mcp.env`, no
    ports) and `cloudflared:2026.10.6` (`tunnel --no-autoupdate run`, `TUNNEL_TOKEN` from `tunnel.env`). Both
    `unless-stopped`.
  - `spikes/mcp/deploy/deploy.sh`: rsyncs the source and compose file, streams `mcp.env` over ssh stdin (0600), extracts
    `tunnel.env` on hoid (0600), then runs `docker compose up -d --build`.
  - `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md` §11 "Deployed on hoid (M0-2b)": layout, the §8 checklist labelled, connector results (U9),
    revoke behaviour, impact on architecture.
  - The stack is running on hoid.
- Acceptance:
  - Compose up, tunnel registered, no host port, other containers unchanged: **pass**.
    - `docker compose -p finbot-spike ps` → finbot and cloudflared both running, `ports=[]`.
    - The cloudflared log shows `Registered tunnel connection connIndex=0..3`.
    - `docker ps` names before and after: chore-chart-web-1, ledger-web, ledger-api, chore-chart-api-1 and
      nginx-proxy-server-app-1 are unchanged, with the same ports, plus the two finbot-spike containers.
  - Public endpoints: **pass**.
    - `curl -i https://finance.hoidlabs.site/mcp` → `HTTP/2 401`,
      `www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://finance.hoidlabs.site/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="mcp"`.
    - The well-known JSON shows the issuer and resource as `https://finance.hoidlabs.site[/mcp]`.
  - claude.ai web connector: **pass**. DCR "Claude", then authorize, callback, `login ok for u_9f51ae389a5c (gen 0)`,
    consent 303, token 200, `POST /mcp -> 200` (log in mcp.md §11).
  - Mobile: **pass**. `hello` worked with no new DCR or sign-in.
  - Revoke: **pass**.
    - `docker compose exec -T finbot /mcp-spike revoke --all` → generation 1.
    - Next call: `POST /mcp -> 401`, then refresh `POST /oauth/token -> 400`. claude.ai then asked to reconnect.
    - Re-auth (gen 1) worked and `hello` succeeded again.
  - mcp.md section: **pass** (§11, labels VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED).
  - Secret check: **pass**.
    - The branch diff, grepped for the `.env` values plus token, email, client-id and 26-character-id patterns → 0 matches.
    - On hoid, `grep -rlFf` with the Google, allowlist, tunnel and claude token values over `~/finbot-spike/mcp`,
      excluding `mcp.env` and `tunnel.env`, gave count 0. The patterns were kept in a 0600 file in /dev/shm and deleted
      afterwards.
    - `docker inspect` `Args`/`Cmd` of both containers: 0 token matches. cloudflared's env holds only `TUNNEL_TOKEN`;
      finbot's holds only its own keys.
  - Tests: **pass**. Spike `go vet ./... && go test ./...` is ok. Root `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...`
    is ok.
- Deviations from brief:
  - The tunnel token comes from a second hoid file, `~/finbot-spike/mcp/tunnel.env` (0600, `TUNNEL_TOKEN` only, extracted
    on hoid, never printed). It is not interpolated from `~/finbot/.env`, because that would also expose the claude token
    to compose and every compose command would then need `--env-file`. This is a second secret file next to `mcp.env`.
  - Revoke used `--all`: the distroless image has no shell to read the email from the env file.
  - ChatGPT was skipped (Brendan has no developer-mode plan), so the RFC 9207 `iss` question is still open. Gemini was
    skipped.
